bilateral electric stimulation from 4 electrodes of 2 sequentially placed electrodes of auditory brainstem implant was successfully performed in a patient with bilateral acoustic neuromas.
the bilateral stimulation from 2 auditory brainstem implants improved the patient's ability to localize sound.

bilateral electric stimulation from 1 auditory brainstem implant and 1 cochlear implant can provide good speech perception in quiet and noisy conditions in patients with neurofi bromatosis type 1 and 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel auditory brainstem implant that can be implanted into the human brain.
the development of a hearing aid for the profoundly deaf that uses the auditory brainstem implant (ABI) as a hearing prosthesis.
the use of auditory brainstem implantation in a patient with bilateral neurofibromatous tumors and a history of meningitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no absolute contraindications to the use of the auditory brainstem implant in patients with NF2.
the auditory brainstem implant is a viable option for patients with neurotrophic deafness.

bilateral electric stimulation from 3 auditory brainstem implants is a safe and effective treatment option for patients with neurofibrromatosis type2.
bilateral stimulation from auditory brain stem implants is feasible, safe and may provide additional benefits in terms of speech perception in noise and sound source localization.

bilateral electric stimulation from 1 to 2 sequentially placed Auditory Brainstem Implants (ABI) is a feasible approach for patients with NF2, and that the benefits of this approach outweigh the disadvantages.

the use of bilateral electric stimulation is feasible and can be used to improve the hearing performance of patients with neurofibroma type 2.
